start.name: Western Desert Gas Complex (WDGC), El-Amreya, Alexandria Governorate
start.coord_basis: Town-center coordinate for the Amreya/El-Amreya locality (Wikipedia infobox, 31°06'16"N 29°45'58"E). No independent facility-gate coordinate is publicly available; WDGC is sited within this locality per Egypt Oil & Gas reporting.

end.name: Al-Amirya (Amreya) LPG/Butane Extraction Plant, Merghem area, Amreya, Alexandria Governorate
end.coord_basis: Same Amreya town-center coordinate (Wikipedia) -- the plant is described only as sited in the Merghem area of Amreya, west of Alexandria; no independent facility-level coordinate found that would separate it from WDGC.

prior_research.sheet_conflicts: StartLocation='Rashid' is substantively wrong, not just a misspelling. Egypt Oil & Gas's 'green light' article confirms this 5km link is a distinct, later spur built specifically to feed the Al-Amirya butane plant, separate from the 70km/30in Rashid-to-WDGC line (that's the sibling row, P6703). Quote: GASCO's original line 'to transfer the gases of the Raven field in the Rashid area to the Western Desert gas complex' has 'a length of 70 km' -- that describes P6703, not this row. This row is described as GASCO's 'phase two': feeding 'the Al-Amirya gas plant with quantities of up to 100 million cubic feet per day from the Raven field.' Rashid town is 40+ km from the Amreya industrial zone -- far too far for a 5km pipe. GEM's StartLocation='Rashid' most likely copy-inherited the field-of-origin label from sibling P6703 rather than describing this segment's physical start point. (Note for whoever handles attribute fields, out of this task's endpoints-only scope: the sourced diameter here is 30in, not the prior suggestion's 18in.)
prior_research.notes: Confirms and firms up a prior ROUTE_PARTIAL suggestion with two additional independent Egypt Oil & Gas articles plus Wikipedia for the town coordinate. WDGC and the Amreya LPG/butane plant are both GASCO facilities co-located in the same Merghem/Amreya industrial zone southwest of Alexandria (the 'GASCO Plants in Western Desert, Amreya Produce 26.6 M tons' piece treats them as a paired complex under one production tally). No independently-sourced facility-level coordinates distinguish the two sites, so both endpoints share the same Amreya town-center coordinate -- a true two-point great-circle line from these coordinates would collapse to ~0km, which accurately reflects that this is a short intra-industrial-zone connector, not a research gap. RouteAccuracy should stay 'low'; a human/GIS pass over satellite imagery of the Merghem/Amreya complex would be needed to actually separate the two sites spatially for a meaningful route line.

start.name: NORPETCO North Bahariya Concession (Abrar/Ferdaus/Ganna/Rawda/Rayan fields), Western Desert, Egypt
start.coord_basis: No individually geocodable point found. North Bahariya Concession (165 sq km lease awarded to NORPETCO 27 Oct 2004) sits onshore the Abu Gharadig Basin in the Western Desert, roughly 190 km SW of Cairo, between El Fayoum and the Qattara Depression. Its constituent fields (Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan) are common Arabic words with no dedicated GeoNames/OSM entries distinguishable from unrelated places of the same name -- checked GeoNames and OpenStreetMap/Nominatim for each field name plus 'North Bahariya' with no reliable match, so no coordinate is asserted for this end.

end.name: Abu Gharadig (Abu El-Gharadig oilfield), Matruh Governorate, Western Desert, Egypt
end.coord_basis: GeoNames gazetteer entry 'Abu al Gharadiq', feature type oilfield, Matruh Governorate, Egypt (29 55'00"N 28 00'00"E).

prior_research.notes: Strong corroboration for the corridor and length, weak for exact endpoints. Egypt Oil & Gas (FY2024/25 results article) reports NORPETCO 'extended a 27 km gas pipeline between NORPETCO's and Khalda Petroleum's fields' at $3.8M cost, enabling gas-for-diesel substitution and ~$12M/yr savings -- the 27 km figure exactly matches the sheet's sheet_length_km=27.0, and this is almost certainly the pipeline in question (a second outlet, African Peace Magazine, republishes the same underlying facts -- likely not fully independent of the original press release, so treat as one primary event corroborated by a re-report, not two independent investigations). Khalda Petroleum (APA/Sinopec JV) operates the 'Abu El-Gharadig Complex' field (offshore-technology.com), which is the natural referent of 'Abu Gharadig' in the pipeline name -- this rules in the hypothesis and rules out the GulfPub Abu Qir (coastal/Alexandria-area) match per the hint. NORPETCO (North Bahariya Petroleum Company) operates the North Bahariya Concession, an eastern extension of the Abu Gharadig Basin with six fields: Abrar, Abrar South, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan (egyptoil-gas.com). Neither article names which specific NORPETCO field or which specific Khalda facility the pipeline physically ties into, and none of the individual NORPETCO field names could be geocoded to a distinct, verifiable point (GeoNames/OSM checks came up empty or matched unrelated places). The Abu Gharadig end is anchored to the GeoNames 'oilfield' point for Abu al Gharadiq (29.917N, 28.0E) -- a plausible but not pinpoint-precise stand-in for Khalda's Abu Gharadig Complex specifically. Given no verifiable coordinate could be established for the NORPETCO-side endpoint, resolved is set to false; a human should use this corridor (NORPETCO North Bahariya fields <-> Khalda's Abu Gharadig Complex, ~27 km apart in the Abu Gharadig Basin/Western Desert) plus internal facility knowledge (e.g. specific NORPETCO field production facility coordinates, if GEM has them) to finalize the start point.

start.name: Wanda gas well (Khalda Petroleum exploration well, Egypt Western Desert — specific concession/block not publicly named)
start.coord_basis: No coordinates or concession/block name published in any source found; location given only as 'Western Desert, Egypt.'

end.name: Unnamed existing Khalda Petroleum production/gathering infrastructure, Western Desert, Egypt
end.coord_basis: Sources state the new pipeline links the well to 'existing infrastructure' but never name the receiving facility, field, or gathering station.

prior_research.sheet_conflicts: The task brief hypothesized an offshore Nile Delta/Mediterranean tieback for Wanda; that hypothesis is NOT supported. All corroborating reporting (Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum, TradeArabia, Zawya, EgyptToday, ArabFinance, and multiple Arabic outlets, all tracing to the same 22 July 2026 Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources announcement) places Wanda ONSHORE in Egypt's Western Desert, operated by Khalda Petroleum (an EGPC/APA Corporation 50/50 JV) — not offshore, not Nile Delta. If the sheet's country/location metadata for P7605 says offshore Mediterranean/Nile Delta, that metadata itself needs review (Baird's call).
prior_research.notes: Found the project: Wanda is a deep gas exploration well (15,000 ft) in Egypt's Western Desert, operated by Khalda Petroleum (50/50 EGPC/APA Corporation JV). Ministry of Petroleum announced (22 July 2026) it began production at 40 mmcf/d, and that Khalda built a new 10-km production pipeline ($2.3M) linking the well to 'existing infrastructure' to fast-track output ahead of national-grid tie-in expected end of July 2026. The reported 10 km pipeline length matches the sheet's stated 10.0 km exactly, strongly confirming this is the right project despite the wrong offshore/Nile-Delta assumption in the task brief. However, every source found (a dozen+ outlets, all derivative of one Ministry press release, checked in English and Arabic) is silent on: (1) which of Khalda's many Western Desert concessions/blocks (e.g. Qarun, Matruh, Shushan, Faghur Basin, Salam, Obaiyed areas) Wanda sits in, (2) the name of the 'existing infrastructure'/facility the new line ties into, (3) any coordinates, and (4) nearby named fields. This is a brand-new discovery (announced ~1 week before this research) with no field development plan, EGAS/EGPC bulletin, or map yet public. Some Arabic outlets (elaosboa.com, egcoop.com) transliterate the well name as 'Watda' (واتدا) — possible alternate spelling of the same well; not enough independent confirmation to recommend renaming the GEM entity. Recommend resolved:false with a corridor note ('somewhere in Khalda's Western Desert concession area, onshore Egypt') rather than fabricated coordinates — revisit once an EGAS annual report or more detailed trade-press follow-up names the specific concession. All 4 route_refs re-verified via url_verifier.py (200 OK).
